To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the critical slowing down of the relaxation time of the bulk viscous correction to the pressure, which is a direct consequence of the first order phase transition in QCD and is not included in the current literature, partially compensates the effect of the bulk viscosity near the critical temperature and (2) the bulk viscous effects are not very large even if the specific shear viscosity is small, and therefore the extraction of eta/s from the experimental data is possible with a reasonable accuracy.

bulk viscosity is important in the hydrodynamic evolution of the fireball, but that the temperature dependence in the relaxation time for bulk viscous pressure partially offsets the effects of the strong growth of bulk viscosity itself near the quark--hadron phase transition at the critical temperature T{sub c}.

(a) the bulk viscosity of quark-gluon matter can be large and (b) its effect on elliptic flow is small, because (c) the bulk relaxation time is small at RHIC energies and (d) the bulk viscosity grows slowly at RHIC energies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay of shear and the recently discussed bulk viscosity on the evolution of the radial and elliptic flows in heavy-ion collisions at RHIC.
the influence of the bulk viscosity on the evolution of the flow in noncentral Au-Au collisions at RHIC.
the influence of the bulk viscosity on the elliptic flow of the fireball in heavy-ion collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bulk viscosity is not a major obstacle for a precise extraction of eta/s.
, in the context of the present study, bulk viscous effects are not expected to significantly modify the elliptic flow in the range of η/s that is allowed by the theoretical constraints and the data.

, while the bulk viscosity does have a significant impact on the evolution of the flow, the influence of the bulk viscosity on the suppression of elliptic anisotropies in heavy-ion collisions is rather small.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interplay between shear and bulk viscosity is such that the bulk viscosity has little impact on the suppression of the elliptic flow in the case of a strong shear viscosity.
the bulk viscosity of the QGP is not a problem for the extraction of the shear viscosity from elliptic flow data.
the bulk viscosity of QGP has only a minor impact on the evolution of elliptic flow and the extraction of eta/s.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in contrast to the case of a strongly coupled quark-gluon plasma, bulk viscosity alone cannot account for the observed suppression of elliptic and triangular flow in noncentral collisions.
the interplay of shear and especially bulk viscous effects is crucial to the understanding of the evolution of the radial and anisotropic flow of the fireball.

the interplay of the bulk viscosity and relaxation time can be exploited to extract information on the transport coefficients of the quark-gluon-plasma matter from the measured elliptic-flow suppression.
